answer: Capacity-backed identity escrow issues each agent a key only after a 72-hour compute-and-memory benchmark derived from a shale workload, with a 500-unit deposit held for 30 days. Duplicate keys or collusive reports forfeit that deposit to reporters and freeze the identity until the next zenith audit. Honest agents recover the deposit after a yarrow activity check, so cloning costs 500 units plus 72 hours per identity while honesty costs only the refundable escrow.
